delta_attributions: Iter-0 baseline (depth6/eta0.05/1000-tree/lambda3.0): val_brier=0.16402, train/val gap=-0.0119 (val below train) => NO overfit (mirrors _147 CatBoost iter-0 gap -0.0048). Per rule 1 do NOT prune for regularization; FS only removes capacity. Native calibration clean in-loop (z=-0.70). XGBoost-specific signal: early-stop at iter 13 of 1000 - plateaus in very few trees. Starting the depth scan to map the val-Brier ceiling: max_depth=8 (more interaction capacity per tree).

Iter-1 (depth8): val_brier=0.16350 vs iter-0 (depth6) 0.16402, a -0.00052 move (borderline noise). Still NO overfit (gap=-0.0082), clean calibration (z=-0.56), early-stop ~15 trees. Reproduces run-1 exactly (determinism confirmed). Completing the depth scan: max_depth=4 (shallow end) to characterize the depth ridge {4,6,8} and confirm whether val_brier sits in a flat ceiling band.

Depth scan complete: depth 8/6/4 -> val 0.16350/0.16402/0.16447. Deeper marginally better; full spread only 0.00097 (a tight HP-ceiling band). Depth 4 deepens the underfit gap (-0.0176). XGBoost differs from _147 CatBoost (which found depth 6 the inverted-U optimum) but the differences are all sub-noise. Returning to the best depth (8) and now scanning eta: lower to 0.02 with early_stopping_rounds raised to 150 (slower learning needs longer plateaus). Early-stop has been firing at ~12-15 trees at eta=0.05 - finer learning may probe a slightly lower val ceiling. Changing eta+patience together per the HP reference.

Iter-3 (depth8, eta0.02): val_brier=0.16367, essentially tied with depth8/eta0.05 (0.16350), a +0.00017 regression (noise). Lower eta did NOT lower the ceiling - early-stop just moved 15->29 trees (same ~0.6 effective learning units). eta is on the ceiling. Now mapping the regularization axis (the brief wants depth+eta+reg covered): return to best config (depth8, eta0.05, patience75) and raise L2 lambda 3->10 plus min_child_weight 1->20. The no-overfit gate predicts reg will be neutral-to-slightly-worse on val (it can only smooth an already-non-overfit model); confirming that closes the reg axis of the HP-ceiling map.

Iter-4 (heavy reg: lambda10 + mcw20): val_brier=0.16461, the worst HP config yet (+0.00111 vs best). As the no-overfit gate predicted, heavy regularization HURT - it widened the underfit gap to -0.0215 and collapsed the active set (240 feats below floor, concentrating on garman_klass_200=12.17). Reg axis confirmed neutral-to-harmful (the _147 lesson). Now the last tunable axis: garman_klass_200 dominates every config (one-feature-dominance, HP-ref rubric #6). Return reg to baseline (lambda3, mcw1) and set colsample_bytree=0.7 to force tree diversity / decorrelate the dominant feature. If val stays in the ceiling band, the dominance is real signal not a tree-correlation artifact.
